newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday December 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday December 18.

text.p: The following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* The parliamentary lower house approved a controversial jumbo package on the broadcasting sector. A measure including in the package extends broadcasting licences until the end of next May for Mediaset, which is owned by opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi. The hard-line Communist Refoundation party voted against the bill (all).

* Leftist PDS party leader Massimo D'Alema, commenting on fierce criticism from communists over the deal on TV, spoke of "suicidal logic" which might give back power to the right. The PDS is a maina party in the centre-left ruling coalition (all)

* Italian parliament cheered the U.S. Supreme Court decision to suspend the execution of death-row inmate Joseph O'Dell. Pope Jean Paul II, President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro and Prime Minister Romano Prodi had all made pleas for clemency (all).

* Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi says the 1997 budget "is enough" to join EMU, after the International Monetary Fund recommended in a letter that the government cracks down on state spending, especially on pensions. "We will prepare an extra budget only if it is necessary" Ciampi said (all).

* In an interview Oliviero Diliberto, leader of Communist Refoundation party in the lower house, says his party is ready for discussion on the welfare state and will not oppose intervention "on those privileges we do not defend" (La Repubblica).

* A meeting was held between Industry, Finance and Labour ministers to seek a compromise in the dispute over metalworkers contract renewals. Giorgio Fossa, chairman of employers association Confindustria participated among others (all).

* The Treasury said it had kicked off a 1.977 trillion lire capital increase for ailing Banco di Napoli. Insurance company INA was ready to bid for a 60 percent stake the state is selling in the bank if the board of Banca Nazionale del Lavoro (BNL) also agrees to participate. The final aim might be a merger between BNL and Banco di Napoli (Il Sole 24 Ore).

* Television and advertising group Mediaset has exercised options to buy 25 percent stakes each in Spain's Gestevision Telecinco SA, Publiespana SA and Estudios Telecinco SA from its parent company Fininvest (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
